initiation.analysts: GAM Research — Financials (NBFCs and financial conglomerates)

cover.headline: A better-run financial conglomerate, but the discount that made it cheap has mostly closed
cover.lead: Aditya Birla Capital (ABCL) is the Birla group's financial-services arm: since April 2025 it is itself a ₹1.67 lakh crore NBFC (ROA 2.4%, Stage 3 1.3%), and it owns 86% of a fast-growing housing-finance company, 51% of a life insurer (with Sun Life), 45% of the listed Aditya Birla Sun Life AMC and 46% of a health insurer. Q1FY27 was strong: group profit +40% to ₹1,175 cr, NBFC AUM +28%, housing loans +50%, life-insurance margin doubled to 15%. The street values ABCL on a **sum of the parts** (₹390-500, all Buy). We do the same: NBFC 2.4x Sep-28E book, HFC 1.8x, the AMC stake at market, the life insurer 1.4x embedded value and the health insurer 1x premium give ₹485 a share before any discount. Since 2022 ABCL has traded anywhere between a 2% premium and a 51% discount to that look-through value (median 17% over the last two years, ~11% today). Applying the two-year median gives **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with HOLD**. Bull {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.h: The NBFC has become a good lender
arguments.p: AUM grew 27% in FY26 and 28% in Q1FY27 with credit cost down to ~1.0% of the book, Stage 2+3 down 127bp in a year to 2.43% and ROA up to 2.39%. The June ₹4,000 cr raise (promoters ₹3,080 cr, IFC ₹920 cr) funds three years of growth. We model AUM +{{F.aumGrowth.0|pct}} / +{{F.aumGrowth.1|pct}} / +{{F.aumGrowth.2|pct}}. What has not come is margin: NIM incl. fees 6.22% (FY25) → 6.07% (Q1FY27).

arguments.h: The rest of the group is improving from a low base
arguments.p: Housing finance: ROA 2.1%, AUM +50%, Advent paid 2.2x post-money book for 14% in April. Life insurance: VNB margin 7.5% → 15.1% YoY, target >20%. Health insurance: profitable under IFRS in Q1 but still a 106% combined ratio. The AMC (9.7% of our gross value) grows slowly and keeps losing equity share.

Our consolidated rebuild gives ROE of 13.1% / 13.2% / 14.1% for FY27-29E against a 13.4% cost of equity; standalone ROE is ~{{F.roe.0|pct}} because ₹9,000 cr sits in subsidiaries at cost. Equity was raised in FY24 and again in June 2026, and partners own 49-54% of the insurers.

At ₹381 the stock trades at 2.0x our FY28E consolidated book against a 1.5x median forward P/B since 2021, and the holding discount has narrowed from ~20% (median since 2022) to ~11%. If the discount stayed at today's ~11%, our value would be ~₹430; at the two-year median it is {{dcf.tp|inr}}, a HOLD. The street's ₹390-500 mostly assumes no discount or a small one.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): first quarter with the full benefit of the June raise; gold loans go live; management expects NBFC margins to rise "in a few more quarters".

IRDAI's insurance-distribution reforms (consultation of 23-Sep-2026, comments due 25-Oct-2026): caps of ~2-5% on loan-linked commission would hit NBFC fee income and change ABSLI's credit-life economics.
RBI's October 2026 policy: most economists polled expected a 25bp repo hike; ~30% of ABCL's borrowings are floating.
Housing finance: ₹1 lakh crore AUM targeted in 6-10 quarters and ROE back to ~13% by Q4FY27 after the Advent dilution.
Health insurance: management aims for a 100% combined ratio (IFRS) in FY27, from 106% in Q1.

sections.title: One listed lender, five partly-owned businesses around it

blocks.p: ABCL started as the Birla group's financial-services holding company (listed 2017). Since its main subsidiary, Aditya Birla Finance, was merged into it on 1-Apr-2025, ABCL is itself the operating NBFC: an RBI "upper layer" lender with ₹1,67,456 cr of loans in June 2026, 463 branches and a AAA rating. Around it sit the businesses it owns with partners. Grasim Industries owns 53.1% of ABCL and other promoter entities 15.7%.

blocks.p: **How the money flows.** Almost all of ABCL's own profit is lending profit: interest income of ₹16,150 cr, fees and commission of ₹679 cr and the AMC's dividend (₹311 cr) in FY26. The insurers pay no dividends; they need capital (₹750 cr into the life insurer in FY26, another ₹950 cr in July 2026, half of it from ABCL). The group reports a consolidated profit that adds its share of the housing-finance company, the life insurer, the AMC and the health insurer, less the digital platform's losses. That consolidated number (₹3,764 cr in FY26, EPS ₹14.41) is what the street forecasts; our lender model covers the standalone company and we rebuild the consolidated figure around it.

blocks.callout: **Why it matters for the stock:** ABCL is a lender wrapped around minority-shared insurance and asset-management stakes. Investors pay for the lender's growth and returns, and they apply a discount to the stakes they cannot control or cash in. That discount, not the NBFC's growth, has driven most of the share price over the last two years.

blocks.p: **What to take from it.** The group has repeatedly raised equity (₹3,000 cr in 2023, ₹4,000 cr in 2026) and sold partial stakes (AMC shares to the public, 10% of the health insurer to ADIA, 14% of the housing-finance company to Advent) to fund growth. Each sale crystallised value at a premium to book (Advent paid 2.2x post-money book), but each also left ABCL with less than full control. The merger with Aditya Birla Finance removed one layer: the lender's equity now sits in the listed company.

sections.title: The NBFC: an MSME lender that is rebuilding its retail book

blocks.p: The NBFC lends to small businesses (57% of AUM: ₹76,319 cr secured against property or receivables, ₹18,780 cr unsecured), to individuals (14%, mainly personal loans with an EIR of ~16.2%) and to mid-sized companies and developers (29%). About 72% of the book is secured. Disbursements were ₹21,201 cr in Q1FY27 (+34%), 72% of them to retail and SME. After 18-24 months of cutting riskier cohorts the personal-loan share fell from ~19% to 12.5% and is now climbing again (14%). Gold loans start in Q2FY27 with ~200 branches by March 2027.

pair.title: MSME loans drive growth; corporate loans grow slowest
Growth by segment, Jun-26 vs Jun-25

blocks.callout: **So what:** growth is broad-based and mostly secured, which is why credit costs fell. The flip side is margin: secured MSME and corporate loans yield less, so a 28% larger book earned a flat NIM. The model assumes AUM growth of {{F.aumGrowth.0|pct}} in FY27E, slowing to {{F.aumGrowth.2|pct}} by FY29E.

sections.title: Spread and NIM: yields fell as fast as funding costs, so margins stood still

pair.title: Company basis: NIM incl. fees ~6.1% for two years
pair.source: ABCL presentations Q4FY23-Q1FY27 (company basis: ratios on the average lending book, NIM incl. fees)

pair.title: Our basis: NIM ~5% of AUM, a little higher after the raise
pair.unit: % of average AUM (yield, NIM) or borrowings (cost of funds), standalone

blocks.p: Two bases are in play. The company quotes margins on the average lending book with fees included (NIM 6.06% in FY26, 6.07% in Q1FY27). Our model uses interest income ÷ average AUM and NII after interest expense (NIM {{fin.nim.11|pct}} in FY26). Both say the same thing: margins peaked in FY24 (6.90% company basis) and have drifted lower as the mix moved to secured MSME and corporate loans. The June raise replaces ~₹4,000 cr of borrowing with equity, worth ~15bp of NIM on our basis in FY27E ({{F.nim.0|pct}}). Beyond that we assume only 5bp a year of yield gain from mix; management's case for more rests on personal loans returning to 18-19% of AUM.

blocks.callout: **The honest read:** margin expansion has been promised for several quarters and has not come (Motilal Oswal called it "contrary to earlier expectation"). We do not bank on it. Each 10bp of NIM is worth ~₹180-200 cr of pre-tax profit in FY27E, about 4% of standalone profit.

pair.title: Our forecast lets credit cost drift back up

blocks.p: Gross Stage 3 fell from 2.27% to 1.30% in a year and Stage 2+3 from 3.70% to 2.43%; 40% of unsecured-business Stage 3 is covered by government guarantee schemes. Coverage on Stage 3 (48%) is modest for a book with unsecured loans, but secured loans carry lower losses. We model credit cost of {{F.creditCost.0|pct}} of AUM in FY27E rising to {{F.creditCost.2|pct}} by FY29E: the benign phase of the cycle will not last for ever, and the book is shifting back to unsecured personal loans.

sections.title: Funding and capital: AAA-rated, well matched, and freshly capitalised

blocks.p: Borrowings were ₹1,42,798 cr in June 2026: term loans, NCDs, commercial paper, ECBs and bank lines, with long-term debt rated AAA by CRISIL, ICRA and India Ratings. ₹9,280 cr of long-term money was raised in Q1FY27. The asset-liability profile shows a cumulative surplus in every bucket up to one year. About 30% of borrowings and 56% of loans are floating, so a rate rise reprices assets faster than liabilities. Capital: Tier 1 of 15.95% and CRAR of 18.82% after the June raise (regulatory minimum 10% / 15%); investments in subsidiaries are deducted from Tier 1.

pair.title: Tier 1 capital back to 16% after the raise
Leverage creeps up again from FY28E

blocks.callout: **Our read:** funding is a strength (group parentage, AAA, diversified lenders) and capital is now comfortable. At our growth rates AUM ÷ equity goes from {{F.leverage.0|n2}}x in FY27E to {{F.leverage.2|n2}}x in FY29E, so the "no raise for three years" promise looks realistic, provided the subsidiaries do not need more from ABCL than the ~₹500 cr a year we assume.

sections.title: Housing finance: from sub-scale to ₹50,000 crore in three years, now with Advent

blocks.p: Aditya Birla Housing Finance (ABHFL) lends to prime and affordable home buyers and against property, with average tickets of ₹25-30 lakh. AUM grew 50% YoY to ₹51,833 cr in June 2026, disbursements 39%; Stage 3 is only 0.41%. Profit doubled to ₹647 cr in FY26 (ROA 1.88%, ROE 14.3%) as cost-to-income fell from 58% to 47%. On 17-Apr-2026 Advent International (through Indriya Ltd) bought 14.3% for ₹2,750 cr at ₹223.12 a share, valuing the company at ₹19,250 cr, 2.21x its post-money book. The extra equity cut ROE to 11.3% in Q1; management expects ~13% by Q4FY27 and 15% in 6-8 quarters, with ₹1 lakh cr of AUM.

blocks.callout: **Valuation:** 1.8x Sep-28E book (₹12,354 cr) for ABCL's 85.5% = ₹70 a share. Listed housing-finance companies trade at ~0.15x book per point of ROE (Bajaj Housing, PNB Housing, Aavas, Aptus, Home First, Aadhar) and have de-rated 32% against their five-year median P/B; at ABHFL's ~15% FY28-29E ROE that is ~2.2x trailing book, or 1.8x on Sep-28E book. Advent's entry price, restated the same way, is ~1.8x. The street uses 1.8-2.2x Mar-28E book.

sections.title: The AMC: a cash cow that is losing ground

blocks.p: Aditya Birla Sun Life AMC (listed, ABSLAMC) managed ₹4.28 lakh cr of mutual-fund assets in Q1FY27 (QAAUM +6% YoY, equity +10%, equity mix 46.5%) and, with mandates, over ₹10 lakh cr after winning a ~₹6 lakh cr EPFO mandate. FY26 PAT was ₹975 cr (+2%) on revenue of ₹1,845 cr; Q1FY27 PAT ₹309 cr (+12%). Its market share of MF assets is 3.97% and it has been losing equity share to faster-growing rivals. For ABCL it is the only business that sends cash up: a dividend of ₹311 cr in FY26.

blocks.callout: **Valuation:** we take the stake at the 30-Sep market price (as for listed stakes in our other holding-company reports) rather than at a target multiple; the holding discount then applies to it like everything else. Brokers use 26-28x earnings, slightly above the 28.5x trailing P/E it already trades on only if earnings grow.

sections.title: Life insurance: margins finally rising, but returns on EV are still mid-pack

blocks.p: Aditya Birla Sun Life Insurance (ABSLI, 51% with Sun Life) wrote ₹24,779 cr of gross premium in FY26 and has ₹1.17 lakh cr of policyholder assets. Individual first-year premium grew 20% in Q1FY27 (private sector 15%). The big change is margin: net VNB margin 15.1% in Q1FY27 vs 7.5% a year earlier (20.6% for FY26) as non-par, protection and annuity products and riders replaced ULIPs. Embedded value was ₹15,447 cr at March 2026 (+12%); operating return on EV was 13.2%, but a ₹934 cr negative economic variance (bond yields) and ₹750 cr of new capital sat in the walk. Management targets 20%+ growth in individual premium and >20% margins for three years, and to double VNB in that time.

sections.title: Health insurance: the fastest-growing SAHI, still not making money

blocks.p: Aditya Birla Health Insurance (ABHI) is a standalone health insurer (SAHI) built around a "health first" model that rewards healthy behaviour with premium refunds. Sales GWP was ₹7,292 cr in FY26 (+39%) and ₹2,196 cr in Q1FY27 (+50%), taking its SAHI share to 16.2%. It moved to IFRS from April 2026: profit ₹61 cr in FY26 and ₹18 cr in Q1FY27, with a combined ratio of 105-106%. ABCL owns 45.9%; Momentum (MMI) 44.1% and ADIA 10.0% (ADIA paid ₹665 cr for 9.99% in 2022, a post-money value of ₹6,650 cr).

pair.title: Group ROE edges up only slowly

blocks.p: **Capital allocation.** In five years ABCL has raised ₹7,000 cr of equity (2023, 2026), sold ~5% of the AMC, brought ADIA into health insurance and Advent into housing finance, and put ₹2,369 cr into subsidiaries in FY26 alone. The money went where returns are highest (the NBFC and HFC); the insurers have absorbed capital for a decade with little cash back. The result is a group ROE stuck near 12-13% while the NBFC earns ~16%. Our FY27-29E consolidated ROE of 13.1-14.1% assumes the insurers' profits rise and the digital platform's losses shrink.

sections.title: The lender has compounded profit ~19% a year; the group less so

blocks.p: Two sets of numbers matter. **The NBFC** (Aditya Birla Finance until April 2025, now ABCL itself) grew profit from ₹1,108 cr in FY22 to ₹3,001 cr in FY26, about 28% a year, while its loan book tripled to ₹1.60 lakh cr. **The group** (consolidated, after partners' shares) earned ₹3,764 cr in FY26, up from ₹1,660 cr-odd in FY22 on Screener's basis but with large one-off gains in between (₹2,739 cr when ADIA invested in health insurance in FY23, ₹433 cr and ₹191 cr from selling AMC shares in FY24-25). Before one-offs, group profit grew from ₹2,057 cr (FY23) to ₹3,797 cr (FY26), ~23% a year. Return on equity has been the weak spot: 12% at group level in FY25-FY26, because the insurers and the AMC tie up equity that earns little or is shared with partners.

pair.title: NBFC profit: ₹1,108 cr to ₹3,001 cr in four years

blocks.callout: **Our view:** the NBFC is a good lender that has finally reached scale (ROA 2.3-2.4%), but ABCL is not just the NBFC. The standalone return on equity ({{F.roe.0|pct}} in FY27E) is held down by ₹9,000 cr of investments in subsidiaries carried at cost, and the group's consolidated ROE (~13% in our FY27-28E rebuild) only just clears a 13.4% cost of equity. Profit growth will be strong (FY27E standalone {{F.patGrowth.0|chg}}, helped by the ₹4,000 cr raise that cuts borrowing), but returns are what the valuation has to pay for.

blocks.p: **How our forecasts compare.** We take management at its word on capital (no raise for three years) and on HFC scale (AUM ₹1,08,000 cr by FY29E), but not on margins: we assume NBFC yields rise only 5bp a year. Our consolidated profit grows 38.7% in FY27E (Q1 +40% off a low base), helped by the June raise and the HFC.

sections.title: Earnings quality: clean lending profits, noisy group profits

bullets: **One-off gains inflate history.** Group profit included a ₹2,739 cr fair-value gain in FY23 (ABHI became a joint venture after ADIA invested) and gains on selling AMC shares of ₹433 cr (FY24) and ₹191 cr (FY25, net of tax). The company's "excluding one-offs" profit is ₹2,057 cr / ₹2,902 cr / ₹3,142 cr / ₹3,797 cr for FY23-26; we use these in the P/E history.

**Two accounting bases in insurance.** ABSLI reports statutory (IGAAP) profit, tiny relative to its embedded value; ABHI moved to IFRS from April 2026 and restated FY26. Neither is a good guide to value, which is why we use EV and premium multiples.
**Restated standalone history.** The merger was accounted from 1-Apr-2024 (FY24 restated); standalone figures before FY24 are the old holding company.

**Screener EPS vs reported EPS.** Screener's consolidated EPS (₹14.75 for FY26) divides profit including minorities by shares; the reported basic EPS is ₹14.41. Our consolidated forecasts are on the owners' basis.
**Fee income is partly insurance commission** on loans, exactly what IRDAI's September proposal would cap; we cut fees by ~6bp of AUM from FY28E.
**Provisioning looks adequate, not generous:** Stage 3 cover of 48%, no management overlay disclosed.

sections.title: A ₹1.7 lakh crore standalone balance sheet, now carrying ₹33,700 cr of equity

blocks.p: At Mar-2026 the standalone company had ₹1,70,586 cr of assets: ₹1,50,635 cr of loans, ₹16,691 cr of investments (of which ₹8,991 cr were its stakes in the housing-finance company, the insurers, the AMC and smaller subsidiaries, at cost) and small fixed assets. It was funded by ₹28,701 cr of equity, ₹1,38,415 cr of borrowings and ₹3,470 cr of other liabilities. In June the ₹4,000 cr preferential issue lifted equity to ₹33,700 cr, Tier 1 capital from 13.8% to 16.0% and cut borrowings ÷ equity from 4.8x to 4.2x. Because the RBI deducts investments in subsidiaries from Tier 1, ABCL needs more equity than a pure lender of the same size.

sections.title: Ownership: Grasim and the Birla family control 69%; domestic funds have replaced foreign ones

blocks.p: Promoters held 68.81% at June 2026 (Grasim 53.1%, other Birla entities 15.7%), foreign investors 7.94%, domestic institutions 13.36% and the public 9.77%. Promoter holding rose from 68.51% (Mar-26) to 68.81% (Jun-26) after the June preferential allotment (Grasim 8.09 cr and Suryaja 0.56 cr of the 11.24 cr new shares; IFC the rest, ~0.9% of the enlarged capital by our arithmetic). Foreign investors fell from 10.9% (Mar-24) to 5.2% (Dec-25) and recovered to 7.9%; domestic institutions rose from 7.6% to 13.4% over the same period.

blocks.p: We are close to the street on profit: consolidated EPS of ₹19.12 / ₹23.28 against Motilal Oswal's ₹18.5 / ₹23.6. Our standalone EPS is above HDFC Securities' mainly because we include the June raise (less interest) and the AMC dividend; their per-share figures look based on the pre-issue share count. The disagreement is not about earnings but about what to pay for them: we apply a holding discount the market itself has applied for most of the last four years.

sections.title: The street is unanimously positive; the sceptics' points are worth hearing

blocks.p: Every broker we found rates ABCL a buy or add, with targets of ₹390-500 (consensus ~₹435 from 14 analysts at end-July). The bull case is simple: a 25%+ growth lender at a 2.3-2.4% ROA, an HFC scaling fast, insurers with rising margins, and consolidated profit growth of ~28% a year. Motilal Oswal's ₹480 has no holding discount; Emkay's ₹400-440 deducts 20% on the subsidiaries.

exhibit.title: Critiques of the bull case, and our view
head: Critique
Our view
rows: A holding company with partners everywhere: Sun Life owns 49% of ABSLI and co-promotes the AMC, Momentum and ADIA own 54% of ABHI, Advent 14% of ABHFL. Cash flows up to ABCL mainly as the AMC dividend (₹311 cr in FY26); insurers need capital, not pay dividends.
Valid: we apply a holding discount and value the AMC at market, not on a target multiple.

Dilution: equity raised in FY24 (preferential to promoters) and again in Jun-2026 (₹4,000 cr at ₹356.02, below the ₹380.60 price on 30-Sep but a premium to the day before the board meeting). Share count up from 241.6 cr (Mar-22) to ~273.7 cr.
Valid: dilution is why per-share value grows slower than group profit.

NBFC margins have not expanded: NIM incl. fees 6.22% (FY25) → 6.06% (FY26) → 6.07% (Q1FY27) as the book tilted to secured MSME and corporate loans; the promised lift depends on personal and consumer loans rising back to 18-19% of AUM.
Valid: we assume only 5bp a year of yield gain.
Group drags: ABHI ran a 105-106% combined ratio in FY26-Q1FY27; the ABCD digital platform lost ₹264 cr in FY26; 'others' cost ₹298 cr of segment PBT in FY26.
Valid: we value ABCD at zero and keep "others" losses at ~₹300 cr a year.
AMC: equity market share has slipped (HDFC Securities); mutual-fund QAAUM grew only 6% YoY in Q1FY27 against a faster industry.
Partly: the AMC is under 10% of our gross value.
Insurance-linked fee income: NBFC fee income rose 60% YoY in Q1FY27 on processing fees and insurance attachment, exactly the income IRDAI's September proposal targets.
Valid: fees cut ~6bp of AUM from FY28E; the bear case doubles that.
exhibit.source: GAM Research

blocks.p: We measure ABCL's discount the way we did for Godrej Industries and GSFC: at every quarter-end since March 2022 (the first March after the AMC listed), ABCL's market value against the look-through value of its parts on our own conventions, with the multiples held at our base case: the NBFC at 2.79x and the HFC at 2.09x book at that date (our 2.4x / 1.8x Sep-28E multiples restated on point-in-time book), the life insurer at 1.4x its latest embedded value, the health insurer at 1x its latest full-year premium, the AMC and broking stakes at that day's price, ARC at book. blocks.callout: **Our judgement.** The discount is structural, not a mistake the market will correct: the insurers and the AMC are shared with partners, pay ABCL little cash, and need capital; the free float is ~31%. It narrowed for good reasons (the merger, better NBFC returns, Advent's price for the HFC), which is why we use the two-year median (17%) rather than the full-period 20%. But at ~11% today the market already gives ABCL most of that credit. A caveat on the method: holding multiples constant means part of the history reflects sector moods (life insurers traded at 3x EV in 2021-22), so we read the level with judgement, not as precise.

blocks.p: **How sensitive the rating is.** Each 0.1x on the NBFC multiple moves value by ~₹10 a share; each 5 points of holding discount by ~₹24. A BUY needs a target of ~₹438 (15% above the 30-Sep price): the discount held near today's ~11% with the NBFC at ~2.6x, or our base multiples with only a ~5% discount. A SELL needs a target below ~₹362: a ~25% discount at our base multiples, or the long-run median with lower multiples.

**Engine note.** Our lender model covers the standalone company only, and the lender engine values lenders on P/E, P/B, justified P/B or residual income, not on a sum of the parts. The SOTP value per share is therefore carried into the engine and the Excel model as an implied multiple of standalone Sep-28E book ({{dcf.blend.methods.0.mult|n2}}x base). In the Excel file the target moves with the NBFC's book; the other parts are fixed inputs from this chapter.

sections.title: Our honest summary: a good business at a fair price, so a HOLD

blocks.callout: **What you are buying:** a ₹1.67 lakh crore NBFC that has fixed its asset quality (Stage 3 1.3%, credit cost ~1%) and now earns a 2.4% ROA, an 86% stake in a housing-finance company growing 50% a year with 0.4% Stage 3, half of a life insurer whose margins have doubled, 45% of a listed AMC and 46% of the fastest-growing health insurer. Capital for three years is in the bank, and the Birla group stands behind it.

**What you are paying:** ₹381 is 2.0x our FY28E consolidated book (median since 2021: 1.5x) and only ~11% below the look-through value of the parts at our multiples, against a 17% two-year median discount and 20% since 2022. Consolidated ROE of ~13% barely clears a 13.4% cost of equity. Our sum of the parts gives {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}).

bullets: **Rating: HOLD, target {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}).** Our ratings follow the upside to our 12−month target: BUY at +15% or more, HOLD between −5% and +15%, SELL below −5%.
**On today's numbers we would turn buyers below ~₹350 and sellers above ~₹420.** The 30-Sep price of ₹381 sits inside the band.
**Biggest swing factors:** the holding discount (5 points ≈ ₹24 a share), the NBFC multiple (0.1x ≈ ₹10 a share) and credit cost (10bp ≈ 3.5% of FY28E standalone profit).

**Portfolio fit:** for investors who want diversified exposure to Indian financial services with a strong parent; not a high-return compounder at group level and not cheap after doubling since March 2025. Size positions for a bear case near {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

sections.title: Glossary

exhibit.title: Terms used in this report
head: Term
What it means
rows: Non-banking financial company; ICC = investment and credit company; the RBI's "upper layer" carries bank-like rules (CRAR ≥15%, Tier 1 ≥10%).
Standalone = ABCL alone (the NBFC, with subsidiaries at cost). Consolidated = the group, adding ABCL's share of each subsidiary's profit and book.
Sum of the parts: each business valued separately and added up for ABCL's stake. Look-through value = that sum before any holding discount.
How far the listed parent trades below the value of its parts, because investors cannot control or cash in the stakes.
Assets under management (the loan book); new loans paid out in a period.
NII, NIM, yield, cost of funds
Net interest income = interest earned − interest paid; NIM = NII ÷ average AUM (company basis: on the lending book, incl. fees).
Loan-loss provisions ÷ average loans; Ind AS buckets for performing, 30-90 days overdue and 90+ days overdue loans; provision cover on Stage 3.
Profit ÷ average assets; profit ÷ average equity; core capital and total capital ÷ risk-weighted assets.

Embedded value = a life insurer's net worth + present value of future profits on policies in force; value of new business written in a year; VNB ÷ new-business premium; operating return on opening EV.
Gross written premium; standalone health insurer; claims + expenses ÷ premium (above 100% = underwriting loss); 1/n = the rule spreading multi-year premiums over the policy term.
Quarterly average assets under management of a mutual fund; systematic investment plan.
Price ÷ book value, embedded value, premium, earnings.
P/B = (ROE − g) ÷ (cost of equity − g); value = book + present value of profits above the cost of equity.
New shares sold to chosen investors (here promoters and IFC); qualified institutions placement; new shares offered to existing shareholders pro rata.

assumptions._note: Aditya Birla Capital, lender model on the STANDALONE accounts (screener.json basis = standalone): since the merger of Aditya Birla Finance (effective 1-Apr-2025, appointed date 1-Apr-2024; FY24 restated) ABCL itself is the NBFC, and it carries its subsidiaries and associates at cost (₹8,991 cr at Mar-26) and receives the AMC's dividend. The consolidated accounts mix ~₹29,000 cr of life-insurance premium and claims with lending income, which the lender engine cannot represent, so the housing-finance company, the insurers, the AMC and the rest are valued outside the engine in a sum of the parts (sotp block below; built in tools/authoring/ABCAPITAL.ctx.js). Consolidated EPS (the street's basis) is rebuilt in the ctx file as model PAT − AMC dividend + share of each subsidiary's profit. AUM = NBFC lending AUM.

history._why: aum = NBFC AUM at March (Q4FY25 and Q4FY26 presentations; FY24 from the Q4FY24 presentation). provisions = impairment on financial instruments in the standalone P&L (Annual Report FY26 for FY25-26; FY25 annual report's restated FY24). feeIncome = Screener standalone revenue less the annual report's interest income: dividends (AMC ₹311 cr in FY26), fees and commission (incl. insurance distribution), fair-value gains, assignment gains and, in FY24-25, the gains on selling AMC shares (₹636 cr and ₹283 cr). Screener revenue is ₹15-40 cr above the annual report in FY24-25 (it adds part of other income).

src.aum: Q4FY26 presentation p19 (4-May-2026); Q4FY25 p24; Q4FY24 p21
src.provisions/fees: Annual Report FY26 standalone P&L (note 27-35); Annual Report FY25 (FY24 restated)

base._why: 2,61,96,06,094 shares at 31-Mar-2026 (Annual Report FY26, directors' report and note on share capital).

assumptions._aumGrowthWhy: NBFC AUM grew 27% in FY26 and 28% YoY in Q1FY27 (5% QoQ) with disbursements +34%. Management has funded three years of NBFC growth with the June raise (87.5% of ₹4,000 cr) and starts gold loans in Q2FY27 (200-300 branches in FY27). We assume 25% / 23% / 21%: a little below the current pace because the book is now ₹1.67 lakh cr, rates were expected to rise and corporate loans (29% of AUM) grow only ~16%.
assumptions._yieldOnAumWhy: Interest income ÷ average AUM was 12.1% in FY25, 11.3% in FY26 and 11.3% annualised in Q1FY27 (company basis incl. fees: 13.10% → 12.68% → 12.58%) as the mix tilted to secured MSME and corporate loans. Management expects yields to rise only once personal & consumer loans (EIR ~16.2%) go from 14% back to 18-19% of AUM, 'a few more quarters'. We add 5bp a year for mix and gold loans.
assumptions._feeIncomePctWhy: Fee and other operating income (incl. the AMC dividend) ÷ average AUM: 0.92% in FY26 (0.71% excluding the ₹311 cr dividend); Q1FY27 ex-dividend run-rate 0.88% after a 60% jump in processing fees and insurance attachment. Build: fees 0.80% / 0.74% / 0.73% (FY28E cut by ~6bp for IRDAI's proposed caps on loan-linked insurance commission) + AMC dividend growing 10% a year (₹342 / 376 / 414 cr = 0.19% / 0.17% / 0.15% of average AUM).
assumptions._costOfFundsWhy: Interest expense ÷ average borrowings: 7.29% in FY26 (company: interest cost 6.62% of the average lending book). AAA-rated; Q1FY27 cost of funds fell 5bp QoQ. Most economists expected a 25bp repo hike in Oct-2026 (30% of borrowings are floating), so we hold FY27E flat and add 5bp in FY28E.
assumptions._opexPctWhy: Operating expenses incl. depreciation ÷ average AUM: 1.90% in FY26 and Q1FY27 (company: 1.93% / 1.95% of the lending book). Gold loans add 200-300 branches in FY27 and ~1,000 over three years, so we add 5-7bp before scale benefits return in FY29E.
assumptions._creditCostWhy: Impairment ÷ average AUM: 1.25% (FY25), 1.10% (FY26), 0.98% annualised in Q1FY27 (company basis 1.03%) after 18-24 months of cohort clean-up; GS3 1.30%, GS2+3 2.43%, PCR 48%. We assume 1.00% in FY27E rising to 1.10% by FY29E as unsecured and personal loans grow again and rates rise.
assumptions._taxRateWhy: FY26 effective rate 25.4% (₹1,059 cr on ₹4,168 cr); new regime 25.17%.
assumptions._payoutWhy: ABCL has never paid a dividend (Screener payout 0% FY15-FY26) and is raising equity to grow.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Non-operating other income ₹112 cr in FY26 and ₹134 cr in FY25 (Annual Report FY26), mainly interest on tax refunds and miscellaneous receipts; Screener shows ₹99 cr after the ₹12 cr labour-code charge.
assumptions._capitalRaiseWhy: ₹4,000 cr preferential allotment at ₹356.02 in June 2026 (11,23,53,236 shares: Grasim ₹2,880 cr on 23-Jun-2026, Suryaja ₹200 cr, IFC ₹920 cr). Management: no further raise needed for three years. ESOP allotments (a few lakh shares a quarter) ignored.

valuation._why: Cost of equity 13.4% (beta 1.15 as for other diversified NBFCs). The engine's justified P/B and residual income run on the STANDALONE book, which carries the subsidiaries at cost and earns only the AMC dividend on them, so they are a floor, not a fair value: sustainable standalone ROE 14% (NBFC ~16% on three-quarters of the book, ~3.5% dividend yield on the rest). The target is the sum of the parts; the engine has no SOTP method for lenders, so the SOTP value per share is carried as an implied multiple of standalone Sep-28E book (written by tools/authoring/ABCAPITAL.sotp.js from the sotp block).

methods.name: SOTP as implied P/B
methods.why: SOTP value per share expressed as a multiple of standalone Sep-28E book (the engine has no SOTP for lenders): NBFC on P/B, ABHFL on P/B, AMC stake at market, ABSLI on P/EV, ABHI on P/GWP, less the holding discount. Multiples are set by tools/authoring/ABCAPITAL.sotp.js; see the valuation chapter.

methods.name: Justified P/B (standalone, subs at cost)
methods.why: (14 − 10) ÷ (13.4 − 10) on standalone Sep-27E book: values the subsidiaries at cost, so it is a floor.

methods.name: Residual income (standalone)
methods.why: Standalone book plus profits above a 13.4% cost of equity; subsidiaries at cost. A floor.

sotp._why: Sum of the parts on the house conventions: lending businesses on P/B of Sep-28E book (the house 12-month-forward basis); insurers on embedded value / premium at the 12-month target date (Sep-27E), because their multiples are trailing; listed stakes at the 30-Sep-2026 close; less a holding discount derived from ABCL's own history (ctx). Multiples derived in ABCAPITAL.ctx.js; a warning prints if these differ from the derivation.

nbfc._investWhy: Mar-26 ₹8,991 cr (Annual Report FY26 note 8); +₹608 cr of rights issues in Jul-2026 (ABSLI ₹484.5 cr, ABHI ₹123.9 cr) and ~₹500 cr a year after for the insurers and the digital platform (GAM estimate; 12.5% of the June raise is earmarked for subsidiaries).

hfc._why: AUM +50% YoY in Q1FY27 to ₹51,833 cr; target ₹1 lakh cr+ in 6-10 quarters at ~15% ROE; we model +39% / +30% / +26%. ROA 1.88% (FY26), 2.12% (Q1FY27); we use 2.0%. Book Mar-26 ₹5,979 cr + Advent's ₹2,750 cr (17-Apr-2026).

amc._why: Listed: ABCL's 12.96 cr ABSLAMC shares at the 30-Sep-2026 close. PAT path for the consolidated build only: +10% a year (FY26 ₹975 cr; Q1FY27 +12% YoY).

life._why: EV ₹15,447 cr at Mar-26 (operating RoEV 13.2%); we compound at 14% (VNB margin 15.1% in Q1 vs 7.5%, management targets >20% and doubling VNB in three years) plus the Jul-2026 rights issue (₹950 cr for 100%, ABCL's ₹484.5 cr). Economic variance (−₹934 cr in FY26) assumed zero.

health._why: Sales GWP ₹7,292 cr in FY26 (+39%), +50% in Q1FY27; we model +38% / +28% / +24%. Combined ratio 105% (FY26), 106% (Q1); management aims at 100% in FY27; IFRS profit ₹61 cr (FY26) → GAM path ₹150 / 300 / 450 cr.

money._why: Listed Aditya Birla Money (BIRLAMONEY) at the 30-Sep close; 5.65 cr shares (₹5.65 cr capital at ₹1 face value, AOC-1).

others._why: ARC at book (₹489 cr, AOC-1); the ABCD digital platform (FY26 loss ₹264 cr) at zero. 'Others' PAT for the consolidated build is the FY26 residual (−₹312 cr: ABCD, broking, ARC, eliminations) held roughly flat.

holdco._why: Derived in ABCAPITAL.ctx.js from ABCL's discount to look-through value at each quarter-end since Mar-2022 (constant multiples); a warning prints if these differ.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: NBFC AUM grows ~26% a year, margins widen as personal loans and gold rise, credit cost stays below 1%, IRDAI softens its caps; ABHFL reaches ₹1 lakh cr with 15% ROE; ABSLI margins move above 20%; the holding discount stays near today's level.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: A rate-hike cycle and a turn in unsecured and MSME credit: AUM growth slows to ~17%, credit cost rises to ~1.5-1.6%, funding costs up 25bp and IRDAI's caps take most loan-linked insurance fees; insurers and HFC de-rate; the holding discount returns to its long-run median.
